title: Finite faithfully flat relative Frobenius of a smooth connected affine group
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $r\geq1$ put $q=p^r$, $C=k[G]$ and $G^{(q)}=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{k,a\mapsto a^q}k)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with the base-changed group operations. The $k$-algebra map $C\otimes_{k,a\mapsto a^q}k\to C$, $c\otimes a\mapsto ac^q$, defines a group-scheme homomorphism $F^r_{G/k}:G\to G^{(q)}$. This homomorphism is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], faithfully flat (flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and surjective), and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. In particular it is a quasi-compact fppf covering: a surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism. The group $G$ need not be reductive or commutative; the trivial group and $p=2$ are included.

source.place: 2.26--2.28 and Proposition 2.29, printed pp.47--49 (relative Frobenius, its iterates and the faithfully flat isogeny for smooth connected groups); literature/stacks-project/varieties.tex, Tag 0CCD (lemma-relative-frobenius-finite) and Tag 0CCG (remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius), for finiteness. Local finite presentation is automatic for these finite-type morphisms between finite-type schemes over a field.

proof.text: Put $\sigma(a)=a^q$ and $D=C\otimes_{k,\sigma}k$. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], choose algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ of $C$ over $k$. Then $x_i\otimes1$ generate $D$ over its second-factor copy of $k$: expand $c$ as a polynomial in the $x_i$ and use $(bc)\otimes a=c\otimes b^qa$. Thus both algebras are finitely generated. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}D$ is precisely the base change of $G$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$, with the stated $k$-structure. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], the unique fibre of the smooth map $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, namely $G$, is reduced. Hence $C$ is reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff].

source.place: Tag 056T, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal; Milne 2.24--2.26, printed pp.46--47; Stacks Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes

proof.text: Every $a\in k$ has a unique $q$th root: existence follows from algebraic closedness applied to $T^q-a$, and uniqueness from $(u-v)^q=u^q-v^q$ in characteristic $p$. Let $\beta=\sigma^{-1}$. It is a ring automorphism. The map $\theta:D\to C$, $c\otimes a\mapsto c\beta(a)$, is a ring isomorphism with inverse $c\mapsto c\otimes1$: it respects the balancing relation since $\beta(b^qa)=b\beta(a)$, and $c\beta(a)\otimes1=c\otimes a$. These formulas also verify multiplicativity. In particular $D$ is reduced. The formula $\varphi(c\otimes a)=ac^q$ is additive, multiplicative, balanced and $k$-linear for the second-factor structure, and $\varphi(z)=\theta(z)^q$ for every finite tensor sum $z$. If $\varphi(z)=0$, reducedness of $C$ gives $\theta(z)=0$ and then $z=0$. Thus $\varphi$ is injective. These calculations use the tensor relations and universal property in [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], applied to $k$ with its two indicated structure maps; $\theta$ is a ring isomorphism, not asserted to preserve the second-factor $k$-structure.

source.place: 2.24--2.26, printed pp.46--47; proof of Proposition 2.29, printed p.49: the field Frobenius is an isomorphism

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] for the coordinate Hopf maps $\Delta,\epsilon,S$ of $C$. Their base changes give the Hopf operations on $D$. If $\Delta(c)=\sum_j u_j\otimes v_j$, then $\Delta_D(c\otimes a)=\sum_j(u_j\otimes1)\otimes_k(v_j\otimes a)$. Therefore $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\Delta_D(c\otimes a)=a\sum_j u_j^q\otimes v_j^q=\Delta(ac^q)$. Likewise $\epsilon_D(c\otimes a)=a\epsilon(c)^q=\epsilon(\varphi(c\otimes a))$ and $\varphi S_D(c\otimes a)=aS(c)^q=S\varphi(c\otimes a)$. Hence $\varphi$ preserves all Hopf maps. By [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor], $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:G\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is a group-scheme homomorphism for the base-changed group law.

source.place: 2.27(a),(b) and 2.28, printed p.48; Hopf-coordinate expansion of the functoriality and product diagrams

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-target-dominant-group-flatness] to $A=D$, $B=C$ and $i=\varphi$. Its field is our algebraically closed $k$; both algebras are finitely generated by Step 1, $D$ is reduced by Step 2, and $\varphi$ is an injective Hopf homomorphism by Steps 2--3. Consequently $C$ is faithfully flat over $D$ through $\varphi$. This is exactly the reduced-target dominant-homomorphism argument in the source, in affine coordinates; it assumes neither commutativity of the group law nor reductivity.

source.place: Corollary 1.69 and Proposition 1.70, summarized in 1.71, printed p.28; Proposition 2.29, proof on printed p.49

proof.text: The morphism of Step 3 is the $r$-fold relative Frobenius: composing its ring map with $c\mapsto c\otimes1$ gives $c\mapsto c^q$, and with $a\mapsto1\otimes a$ gives the structure map of $C$. Under the affine fibre-product identification of Step 1 these are exactly the defining two projections of the relative Frobenius in [lem-trf-relative-frobenius-finite]. Since $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type, hence locally of finite type, apply that node with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $X=G$ and $n=r$ to obtain finiteness of $F^r_{G/k}$. The characteristic condition holds because $C$ is a $k$-algebra and $p=0$ in $k$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], Step 4 makes $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ surjective. To verify scheme flatness explicitly, faithful flatness implies flatness by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. For $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, localization of $C$-modules is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]; hence $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $D$: tensor an injection with $C$ and localize it, using the fraction identification $(N\otimes_D C)_{\mathfrak q}=N\otimes_D C_{\mathfrak q}$. This identification sends $(n\otimes c)/s$ to $n\otimes(c/s)$, with the evident inverse. Now [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] makes $C_{\mathfrak q}$ flat over $D_{\mathfrak p}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](1), these are the local rings. The stalk map sends $a/t$ to $\varphi(a)/\varphi(t)$ because its composite with the germ map of $D$ sends $a$ to the germ of $\varphi(a)$; the fraction formula is forced since denominators are units. Thus $F^r_{G/k}$ is flat at every point by [def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: Tags 00HB (definition-flat), 00CS (proposition-localization-exact), 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), and 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings); passage to stalks of affine schemes

proof.text: By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], the finitely generated $k$-algebra $D$ is Noetherian. The single affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}D$ therefore makes $G^{(q)}$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Finiteness from Step 5 and [pqf-lem-finite-fp-locnoeth] give finite presentation, in particular local finite presentation as in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finiteness also includes affineness by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) gives quasi-compactness. Together with Step 6 this is the required quasi-compact fppf covering. For the trivial group, $C=k$ and the same formulas give an isomorphism; for $p=2$ every displayed Frobenius identity still holds. No step uses reductivity, commutativity, or a positive group dimension.

source.place: Tags 00FN (Algebra, lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 01OV (Properties, definition-locally-Noetherian), 01TX (lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation); affine morphism permanence
